title: Temperature Scaling Calibration: Bridge 0.22062 → 0.21 NBA Brier Gap
key_insight: IEEE 2026 benchmark: LogReg achieves Brier 0.199 vs XGBoost 0.202 vs CNN 0.221. Our extra_trees fleet best is 0.22062. The LogReg advantage is NOT model complexity — it is native probability calibration. Temperature scaling is a simple post-processing step that can close this gap without retraining.
mechanism: Divide logit outputs by learned scalar T before sigmoid: P_cal = sigmoid(logit(P_raw) / T). T is learned by minimizing NLL (negative log-likelihood) on a holdout set via scalar optimization. T > 1 softens overconfident predictions; T < 1 sharpens underconfident ones.
expected_brier_gain: 0.002 to 0.008 absolute improvement on walk-forward test

implementation.complexity: LOW — 10-20 lines of code, no retraining required
implementation.target_island: S15 (Nomos42/nba-evo-6) — holds fleet best checkpoint at gen 1306
steps: 1. Load champion model checkpoint from S15 (gen 1306, extra_trees)
2. Generate raw probability outputs on 20% holdout set
3. Find optimal T via scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar minimizing NLL on holdout
4. Apply P_cal = expit(logit(P_raw) / T) at inference
6. If Brier improves > 0.001, wrap as post-processing step in engine.py predict()
implementation.code_sketch: from scipy.special import logit, expit; from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar; T = minimize_scalar(lambda t: -np.mean(y*np.log(expit(logit(p)/t)+1e-9) + (1-y)*np.log(1-expit(logit(p)/t)+1e-9)), bounds=(0.1,10), method='bounded').x

secondary_techniques: Platt scaling (logistic regression on raw outputs) — alternative to temperature scaling
Isotonic regression calibration — non-parametric, better for larger datasets
Shot-zone spatial embeddings (rolling-form + shot-chart) from MDPI uncertainty paper
MC-dropout uncertainty bands — enables reject-option betting (only bet when uncertainty < threshold)

applicability.nba_islands: Apply to S15 fleet-best checkpoint first, then roll to S14/S18 if improvement confirmed
applicability.political_islands: Directly applicable — political predictions have same calibration issue (Brier 0.25 vs theoretical optimum ~0.20)
